sources.title: Configure macros to improve representative productivity
Configure Microsoft Teams chat in Customer Service
App profile manager JavaScript API Reference
Add the Knowledge Base Search control to forms
View the communication panel for conversations

questions.prompt: A standalone workspace team needs different pane tools from other representatives. The administrator intends to edit the supplied default profile for just that team. Which approach meets the requirement?
questions.answer: Create a custom profile, configure its tools, and assign the intended team members.
questions.explanation: Use a custom experience profile for a team-specific configuration rather than modifying an immutable supplied default.

options.text: Edit the default profile and expect its changes to apply only to the selected queue.
Create a second queue and leave all experience-profile associations unchanged.
Create a custom profile, configure its tools, and assign the intended team members.
Set the new profile as the global default and expect the changed tools to apply only to one queue team.

optionExplanations.o1: Supplied profiles cannot be modified for this targeted customization.
optionExplanations.o2: Queue membership is not experience-profile selection.
optionExplanations.o3: Custom profiles provide targeted experiences and user assignment.
optionExplanations.o4: A global default associates available users broadly; it does not implement the requested team-specific assignment.

questions.prompt: A new custom profile has the requested pane features, and an assigned test user sees them. Another intended representative still receives the supplied default experience. Permissions are verified. Which check most directly addresses this difference?
questions.answer: Search by user and verify that representatives custom-profile association.
questions.explanation: Verify effective user association when a correct custom profile works for one user but another receives a default.

options.text: Search by user and verify that representatives custom-profile association.
Change session-template panel settings before checking which profile the affected user receives.
Change queue membership and assume that automatically selects this custom experience profile.
Assign additional table privileges despite the verified feature permissions.

optionExplanations.o1: Unassigned users receive a supplied default; user search helps verify association.
optionExplanations.o2: Those session settings do not verify the effective user-to-profile association.
optionExplanations.o3: Queue membership is not a substitute for verifying the profile association.
optionExplanations.o4: More privileges do not select the intended profile.

questions.prompt: An enabled standalone custom-profile inbox should give representatives a new view containing conversations and email. In testing, the configured view contains only conversations and does not appear to the intended users, although their profile association and existing inbox views work. Which TWO view settings should the administrator inspect? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Include email among the view record types. Set Representative visibility to Show.
questions.explanation: Inbox content selection and representative visibility are separate configuration decisions.

options.text: Select only email as the record type and omit conversations from the view.
Include email among the view record types.
Change only the existing conversations filter and leave record types unchanged.
Set Representative visibility to Show.
Add an email condition while retaining only the conversation record type in the view.

optionExplanations.o1: The requirement needs both record types, not replacement of conversations.
optionExplanations.o2: The view must include the requested record types.
optionExplanations.o3: Conversation filtering does not add the missing email record type or make a hidden view visible.
optionExplanations.o4: Show makes the configured view visible to representatives.
optionExplanations.o5: A filter condition does not replace including the email record type.

questions.prompt: A standalone inbox conversation view has correct membership and visibility. Representatives need a supported business-priority attribute to determine display order without changing which conversations appear. Which configuration meets this requirement?
questions.answer: Configure the inbox view Sort entity, attribute and sort order.
questions.explanation: Keep inclusion logic separate from ordering; configure the view custom sort for the supported business attribute.

options.text: Exclude lower-priority conversations through a Simple filter.
Change voice queue priority while retaining the inbox view sort.
Display the priority field but retain the existing date-only sort.
Configure the inbox view Sort entity, attribute and sort order.

optionExplanations.o1: This changes the matching set rather than its order.
optionExplanations.o2: Queue routing priority does not configure the inbox view display order.
optionExplanations.o3: Displaying a field does not select it as the sort.
optionExplanations.o4: The inbox supports custom attribute-based sorting.

questions.prompt: A team enables the inbox and expects accepted voice calls to remain only as inbox cards, without opening sessions. Which behavior should its acceptance test actually expect?
questions.answer: A voice call opens a new session and also adds an inbox card for awareness.
questions.explanation: Inbox awareness and a live voice session coexist; enabling the inbox does not convert voice into an inbox-only interaction.

options.text: A voice call waits as an unaccepted inbox-only record until promoted manually.
A voice call opens a new session and also adds an inbox card for awareness.
A voice call reuses the currently focused chat session instead of creating its own session.
A voice call opens a new session only when the representative is outside the inbox.

optionExplanations.o1: The documented voice behavior creates a new session.
optionExplanations.o2: Voice calls always open a session with an awareness card.
optionExplanations.o3: The documented voice behavior always opens a new session.
optionExplanations.o4: Voice session creation is not conditional on whether the representative is currently using the inbox.

questions.prompt: A standalone Dashboard application tab resolves to the default dashboard even though the requested system dashboard exists, its GUID is correct, and the user has access. Which application-packaging check directly matches the documented fallback behavior?
questions.answer: Include the intended dashboard in the app module definition.
questions.explanation: A valid GUID is insufficient if the dashboard is absent from the application module.

options.text: Include the intended dashboard in the app module definition.
Make the intended dashboard the users personal default and rely on personal-default support in this page type.
Use the entity-list viewId parameter in place of dashboardId while retaining Dashboard as page type.
Clear dashboardId so the default dashboard can infer the intended dashboard.

optionExplanations.o1: A dashboard excluded from the module falls back to the default.
optionExplanations.o2: Personal default dashboards are not supported for this application-tab page type.
optionExplanations.o3: Dashboard and entity-list page types have different parameter contracts.
optionExplanations.o4: A blank ID also falls back to the default.

questions.prompt: A standalone app has one workflow that intentionally opens a new customer form and another that must open an existing customer by supplied ID. A stale ID in the lookup workflow must never silently become a new customer. Which design preserves these business intents?
questions.answer: Keep explicit create configuration for the new-record flow and validateRecord=true for the existing-ID lookup.
questions.explanation: Separate intentional creation from existing-record lookup, and validate existence where stale identity must not open create mode.

options.text: Treat a failed lookup as an intentional create in both workflows.
Use a different formId for lookup and assume it validates the supplied identity.
Remove entityId from both workflows so each follows create-form behavior.
Keep explicit create configuration for the new-record flow and validateRecord=true for the existing-ID lookup.

optionExplanations.o1: The existing-record flow expressly forbids silent creation.
optionExplanations.o2: Form choice does not enforce record existence.
optionExplanations.o3: This converts lookup intent into creation.
optionExplanations.o4: Entity-record configuration distinguishes intentional creation from existing-record lookup and existence validation.

questions.prompt: An iframe-compatible supplier site accepts a case number in its query string. A standalone tab must reuse one template across case sessions rather than hard-code a test case. Which TWO parameter choices implement the documented composition? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Set the URL parameter to the HTTPS supplier URL and fixed query prefix. Use the data parameter with the current anchor case ticket-number slug.
questions.explanation: Combine a valid HTTPS address with supported runtime data rather than cloning a fixed customer URL.

options.text: Set the URL parameter to the HTTPS supplier URL and fixed query prefix.
Hard-code the current test case number in each URL and clone the template for every case.
Use the data parameter with the current anchor case ticket-number slug.
Use an OData query without filtering it to the anchor case and assume it selects the current case.
Use a constant test-case value as data and expect the fixed URL prefix alone to supply runtime identity.

optionExplanations.o1: The URL supplies the required address and fixed query structure.
optionExplanations.o2: Per-case copies violate the reusable runtime composition requirement.
optionExplanations.o3: The optional data parameter can resolve a runtime anchor value.
optionExplanations.o4: An unscoped query does not establish the intended anchor-record value.
optionExplanations.o5: The URL prefix does not replace the required contextual data parameter.

questions.prompt: A standalone team proposes an Entity session template for an organization-owned custom table. The table is available elsewhere in the app and the administrator has required access, but it is absent from the template Entity list. Which documented restriction explains the design boundary?
questions.answer: The Entity list displays user-owned tables only; review the proposed design against that ownership scope.
questions.explanation: Table ownership constrains the Entity session selector; app visibility and broad permissions do not remove that scope.

options.text: Entity templates support every table after a notification template is associated.
The Entity list displays user-owned tables only; review the proposed design against that ownership scope.
Configuring an entity-record anchor tab is sufficient to make any table appear in the Entity session selector.
Broader administrator privileges make all organization-owned tables appear in this selector.

optionExplanations.o1: Notification selection does not remove the ownership scope.
optionExplanations.o2: The procedure explicitly limits this list to user-owned tables.
optionExplanations.o3: An application-tab configuration does not remove the selector ownership restriction.
optionExplanations.o4: The access is verified; ownership is the documented list restriction.

questions.prompt: A standalone chat session must start with its communication panel minimized while keeping the same anchor and additional tabs. Which change belongs in the session template?
questions.answer: Set Communication panel mode to Minimized.
questions.explanation: Initial communication-panel presentation is a session-template setting, separate from notification display and tab composition.

options.text: Change the notification template Show timeout value.
Set desktop-notification delivery to show alerts only when the app is out of focus.
Set Communication panel mode to Minimized.
Minimize the panel manually in each test without changing its initial template mode.

optionExplanations.o1: Notification timer display does not set panel mode.
optionExplanations.o2: Desktop delivery conditions do not set the initial session communication-panel mode.
optionExplanations.o3: This setting controls the initial panel state.
optionExplanations.o4: Manual interaction does not configure the required starting mode.

questions.prompt: A standalone representative clicks the body of a desktop conversation alert rather than its Accept button. Which outcome should an acceptance test expect before the representative makes any further choice?
questions.answer: The app becomes active and shows the in-app request for an accept or reject decision.
questions.explanation: Desktop alert activation and conversation acceptance are separate actions; test the button and body paths separately.

options.text: The app becomes active and shows the in-app request for an accept or reject decision.
Any body click is equivalent to accepting the incoming conversation.
The body click rejects the request and prevents its later acceptance.
The body click starts the customer session without an acceptance decision.

optionExplanations.o1: The documentation distinguishes body activation from the accept/reject buttons.
optionExplanations.o2: A body click activates the app without accepting the request.
optionExplanations.o3: The request remains available for a decision.
optionExplanations.o4: Session start follows acceptance rather than app activation alone.

questions.prompt: A Customer Service record-routing team adds a Reject button to its custom notification and expects this to stop the routed record being assigned. Which TWO statements should guide the design review? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: The routed record is assigned even if a reject option is present. Microsoft recommends omitting Reject for custom record-routing notifications.
questions.explanation: Do not use a Reject affordance as a record-assignment control when the documented routing semantics still assign the record.

options.text: The record remains unassigned until the representative explicitly accepts its notification.
The routed record is assigned even if a reject option is present.
Selecting Reject automatically routes the record back to a queue instead of preserving its assignment.
Microsoft recommends omitting Reject for custom record-routing notifications.
Reducing the notification countdown guarantees that the routed record stays unassigned on expiry.

optionExplanations.o1: The documented warning states the routed record is assigned even if a reject option is provided.
optionExplanations.o2: The documentation explicitly warns of this behavior.
optionExplanations.o3: The guide does not make this affordance a record rejection/rerouting control.
optionExplanations.o4: This is the documented recommendation for these notifications.
optionExplanations.o5: Countdown duration does not remove the documented routed-record assignment behavior.

questions.prompt: A standalone representative receives in-app requests but no native desktop alerts. Desktop notifications are enabled in the application and work for a peer. The browser is supported and not incognito, and OS focus restrictions are excluded. Which remaining delivery prerequisite should be checked on the affected site/browser?
questions.answer: Allow browser notifications for the application site.
questions.explanation: Verify the browser delivery permission separately from the application notification configuration.

options.text: Raise Countdown.
Reenable desktop alerts in the template but keep the browser site permission denied.
Switch from out-of-focus alerts to always-on alerts while retaining browser denial.
Allow browser notifications for the application site.

optionExplanations.o1: Increasing lifetime does not authorize native browser notifications.
optionExplanations.o2: The app setting is already enabled and does not override site permission denial.
optionExplanations.o3: Delivery policy does not remove the browser permission requirement.
optionExplanations.o4: The browser must be allowed to show notifications.

questions.prompt: Several standalone product scripts must reuse the same reviewed escalation guidance. That guidance exists as a separate script. The team wants to maintain it once and open it from a step without duplicating its text or treating it as a data-action macro. Which design fits?
questions.answer: Use Action Type Script and select the escalation guide as Target script.
questions.explanation: Use a script-to-script target for reusable guidance; text instructions and data-action macros do not provide that same composition.

options.text: Copy the guidance text into every product script and maintain every copy.
Use Action Type Script and select the escalation guide as Target script.
Use Text instruction and assume mentioning the guide name opens it automatically.
Use Action Type Macro and select the guidance script as an executable macro.

optionExplanations.o1: Copies fail the single-maintenance requirement.
optionExplanations.o2: A script step can select another configured script through its target lookup.
optionExplanations.o3: Instruction text is not an executable script target.
optionExplanations.o4: A script and an automation macro have distinct action contracts.

questions.prompt: A standalone script currently tells representatives to prepare an acknowledgment email. An existing tested macro performs that operation. The team wants the step to invoke that macro instead of merely displaying the instruction. Which TWO step settings provide that wiring? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Set Action Type to Macro. Select the existing macro in Target macro.
questions.explanation: Guidance and execution are different step contracts; an executable macro step needs its action type and target.

options.text: Set Action Type to Macro.
Grant the representatives the authoring role while leaving this step as a nonexecuting text instruction.
Set Action Type to Text instruction and assume the text runs the macro.
Select the existing macro in Target macro.
Select a Target script with the same display name instead.

optionExplanations.o1: The action type must be executable macro.
optionExplanations.o2: Additional authoring access does not wire an instruction step to invoke the macro.
optionExplanations.o3: Text instruction remains guidance.
optionExplanations.o4: The target lookup selects the configured macro to execute.
optionExplanations.o5: A script target is a different action type.

questions.prompt: A standalone session correctly selects its normal warranty guide by default. Both warranty and exception scripts are already associated with the session type. During one unusual conversation the representative needs the exception guide, while all other sessions must keep their current default. What should the implementation support?
questions.answer: Let the representative manually select the available exception script for this session.
questions.explanation: A correct context-sensitive default does not prevent manual selection of another associated guide for an individual exception.

options.text: Change the shared default expression for all conversations.
Remove the warranty guide from the session template for every representative.
Create a new customer-specific template and replace the shared association.
Let the representative manually select the available exception script for this session.

optionExplanations.o1: A shared change exceeds the one-conversation exception.
optionExplanations.o2: Removal unnecessarily affects other sessions.
optionExplanations.o3: A customer-specific template is unnecessary for an available associated guide.
optionExplanations.o4: Representatives can switch among scripts available for their session.

questions.prompt: A standalone script author can create scripts but cannot select a required language from the Language list. Translating a step name has not added it. Which environment setting should be checked?
questions.answer: Whether that language is enabled in Microsoft Dataverse.
questions.explanation: The authoring language list follows Dataverse-enabled languages rather than text in step or template names.

options.text: Whether that language is enabled in Microsoft Dataverse.
Whether translating a script step automatically enables that language in the environment.
Create another translated script and assume the new record itself enables its language in Dataverse.
Whether the representative browser language alone controls the available script authoring languages.

optionExplanations.o1: The list contains languages enabled in Dataverse.
optionExplanations.o2: Translated text does not enable a Dataverse language.
optionExplanations.o3: Script content does not enable an environment language for the authoring list.
optionExplanations.o4: The documented list follows enabled Dataverse languages, not only browser preferences.

questions.prompt: A standalone case identifies its customer as a contact. A task macro needs that contacts email, which is stored on the related contact rather than as a case attribute. An unrelated account is open in an additional tab and must not change which customer is used. Which input design matches the documented pattern?
questions.answer: Query contact email using the anchor cases customer lookup ID as the filter.
questions.explanation: Scope the related-record query with the anchor customer relationship; the anchor does not automatically contain every field of that related contact.

options.text: Query the unrelated focused account and use its values as the case customer.
Query contact email with contactid filtered by the anchor case ID rather than its customer lookup ID.
Query contact email using the anchor cases customer lookup ID as the filter.
Read an anchor case email attribute and assume every related contact field is already part of the case context.

optionExplanations.o1: The additional account is explicitly not the related customer.
optionExplanations.o2: The query must identify the related contact, not use the case record identity as contactid.
optionExplanations.o3: The documented OData pattern uses anchor customer identity to retrieve related contact values.
optionExplanations.o4: Related contact attributes require retrieval; they are not automatically promoted into anchor case attributes.

questions.prompt: A standalone macro must retrieve the name of an account deliberately selected in an additional tab, not the anchor case customer. Which TWO documented techniques supply the intended additional-record data? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Use Session.CurrentTab entity identity for the focused record. Use the current-tab record ID in a supported OData query for its other values.
questions.explanation: Select the correct record identity first, then query the needed values rather than treating the entire additional record as anchor data.

options.text: Read anchor case customer attributes and assume they represent the focused account.
Use Session.CurrentTab entity identity for the focused record.
Filter an account query by the anchor cases customer identity even though the requirement targets a different focused account.
Assume every field of every additional tab is copied into anchor context.
Use the current-tab record ID in a supported OData query for its other values.

optionExplanations.o1: The requirement explicitly targets the additional record instead of the anchor customer.
optionExplanations.o2: CurrentTab exposes entity name and ID.
optionExplanations.o3: The required account is the additional-tab record, not the explicitly excluded anchor customer.
optionExplanations.o4: The documentation does not populate anchor context with all additional record attributes.
optionExplanations.o5: The documented query pattern retrieves related values from that record identity.

questions.prompt: A standalone macro opens a new task with Regarding pointing to the current case. The designer passes only the case display title as the lookup attribute. Which input design matches the documented lookup pattern?
questions.answer: Supply the related record ID, record type, and record name as separate attributes.
questions.explanation: A lookup is structured identity, not a plain label. Use the documented related-record attributes together.

options.text: Pass only the case title, because lookup display text uniquely identifies the record.
Pass only the record GUID and omit lookup record type and name.
Supply the record ID and type but omit the related record name.
Supply the related record ID, record type, and record name as separate attributes.

optionExplanations.o1: A label alone does not provide the documented lookup structure.
optionExplanations.o2: The action requires the documented triplet.
optionExplanations.o3: The documented lookup pattern includes the related record name as a separate attribute.
optionExplanations.o4: The pattern supplies ID, type and name separately.

questions.prompt: A standalone macro opens a task form, populates details and already includes Save the record. Save fails, and the form validation highlights mandatory task inputs before the next action can proceed. Which correction follows the documented Save action contract?
questions.answer: Populate all mandatory task fields before Save runs.
questions.explanation: The Save action must satisfy required-field validation; repeating a failed save does not repair missing mandatory data.

options.text: Add a second Save action with the same incomplete values.
Populate all mandatory task fields before Save runs.
Open another task form while leaving the original required values blank.
Retry Save after changing only optional task details while leaving the highlighted input mappings unchanged.

optionExplanations.o1: A repeated Save does not satisfy required fields.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented action requires mandatory fields to be entered.
optionExplanations.o3: A second form does not complete the original records mandatory values.
optionExplanations.o4: Optional data changes do not repair missing mandatory field values.

questions.prompt: A standalone macro opens a new form, then a later action needs the tab identifier produced by that first action. The author also wants to paste that action-output reference into a reusable notification template. Which assessment follows the automation dictionary documentation?
questions.answer: Use the first actions output for later macro actions, but do not treat macro-action outputs as template parameters.
questions.explanation: Respect the scope of action-generated context: macro chaining supports it, reusable templates do not inherit that action execution.

options.text: Use the first actions output for later macro actions, but do not treat macro-action outputs as template parameters.
Use the output only in the notification template, never in later macro actions.
Expect every template to execute the macro automatically to obtain its output.
Replace the output with a fixed tab ID taken from an unrelated session.

optionExplanations.o1: Macro action context can feed later actions and is not applicable to templates.
optionExplanations.o2: This reverses the documented scope.
optionExplanations.o3: Templates do not automatically execute the macro to generate an action output.
optionExplanations.o4: A hard-coded unrelated runtime identifier fails the contextual requirement.

questions.prompt: A standalone automation must focus a known session tab and separately invoke a Power Automate flow. Which TWO connector selections align with these operations? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Session connector for the tab operation. Flow connector for invoking the Power Automate flow.
questions.explanation: Choose the connector that owns each operation instead of using one vaguely related automation surface for both.

options.text: Omnichannel connector solely for focusing any workspace tab.
Session connector for the tab operation.
Flow connector solely for setting focus to a known workspace tab.
Flow connector for invoking the Power Automate flow.
Omnichannel connector as the documented direct Power Automate flow trigger.

optionExplanations.o1: The documented session connector owns tab operations.
optionExplanations.o2: It supports tab identifiers, refresh and focus.
optionExplanations.o3: Tab focus is a session connector operation, not flow invocation.
optionExplanations.o4: The flow connector triggers a Power Automate flow.
optionExplanations.o5: The documented flow invocation connector is Flow connector.

questions.prompt: A custom productivity tool works in the source standalone environment. After its configuration is imported into a target, the target setup cannot resolve the referenced custom page or PCF component. User roles and intended profile assignments are verified. Which deployment dependency should the engineer check?
questions.answer: Deploy and publish the referenced custom page or PCF control in the target.
questions.explanation: Component availability is a prerequisite to tool registration and profile rollout; configuration records do not build the referenced component.

options.text: Add another pane-tool configuration pointing to the same absent component.
Grant a broader user role and leave the target component undeployed.
Deploy and publish the referenced custom page or PCF control in the target.
Enable only the tool toggle and assume registration creates its referenced component.

optionExplanations.o1: A duplicate reference does not deploy the component.
optionExplanations.o2: Permissions do not create the missing artifact.
optionExplanations.o3: The component must already exist and be published before it can be referenced.
optionExplanations.o4: Tool enablement does not build its referenced page/control.

questions.prompt: A standalone custom productivity page is visible, but its designer assumed it would automatically know the current case and conversation as the representative switches sessions. Which design correction follows the documented custom-tool limitation?
questions.answer: Implement explicit programmatic passing of the required session context.
questions.explanation: Visible custom tools are standalone experiences; current-session data is not automatically provided by registration or global availability.

options.text: Register a custom tool and assume registration injects all active-record values.
Make the tool global and assume that automatically binds current case data.
Reuse a built-in tools automatic context behavior and assume the custom page receives it without integration.
Implement explicit programmatic passing of the required session context.

optionExplanations.o1: Registration does not establish automatic session context binding.
optionExplanations.o2: Global availability does not provide automatic contextual binding.
optionExplanations.o3: Custom tools do not automatically inherit the contextual binding of built-in tools.
optionExplanations.o4: Custom tools need an explicit context integration design.

questions.prompt: Teams chat is enabled for the standalone workspace app. A targeted team uses a custom multisession profile and custom security roles. Which TWO checks address the documented profile and permission layers before user acceptance? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Enable the feature for the intended custom profile. Verify user permissions equivalent to the Productivity tools user role.
questions.explanation: Validate both the targeted custom profile and user permission prerequisites; app-wide enablement alone is incomplete.

options.text: Enable the feature for the intended custom profile.
Treat existing app-wide enablement as sufficient even with the custom profile unconfigured.
Assign equivalent pane privileges but leave the intended custom profile disabled for the feature.
Skip pane permissions because the app-wide toggle supplies every user privilege.
Verify user permissions equivalent to the Productivity tools user role.

optionExplanations.o1: Specific multisession users require their custom profile feature configuration.
optionExplanations.o2: The documentation requires enabling the feature for the intended custom multisession profile.
optionExplanations.o3: Permissions alone do not complete the feature configuration layer.
optionExplanations.o4: App configuration does not replace required user permissions.
optionExplanations.o5: The documentation specifies this permission equivalence for multisession.

questions.prompt: A standalone representative connects a Teams chat to a case and includes an introduction note from a configured view. A colleague cannot open the case but can read fields included in that note. The team must avoid exposing restricted context through shared text. Which review is appropriate?
questions.answer: Limit the introduction-note fields because its static fields do not check each collaborators field-level permissions.
questions.explanation: Review the static Teams introduction note separately from linked-record access; included context fields can expose information the initiating representative could view.

options.text: Assume denied case access automatically redacts every included note field.
Limit the introduction-note fields because its static fields do not check each collaborators field-level permissions.
Grant every chat participant full case access instead of reviewing the shared note fields.
Remove unsupported field types only and assume every remaining supported field is filtered by each collaborators field-level permissions.

optionExplanations.o1: Record permissions do not automatically filter these static note contents per collaborator.
optionExplanations.o2: The documentation explicitly warns that static context fields do not check collaborator field-level permissions.
optionExplanations.o3: Broadening access fails the restricted-context requirement.
optionExplanations.o4: The supported-field-type behavior does not remove the separate warning that static fields do not check collaborator field-level permissions.

questions.prompt: In a standalone custom app with Teams chat enabled, representatives can connect chats to accounts but need the same capability for a custom service record type. The custom table and user permissions are ready. Which configuration extends the supported connection list?
questions.answer: Add the custom record type under Connect chats to Dynamics 365 records.
questions.explanation: Configure the collaboration record-type integration rather than treating general app enablement as coverage for every custom record.

options.text: Add the custom record type under Connect chats to Dynamics 365 records.
Enable the custom table in the inbox and assume that also adds it to Teams record connections.
Publish another app profile without configuring record-type connections.
Enable knowledge management for the custom record type without configuring Teams connections.

optionExplanations.o1: The documented connection configuration includes custom record types.
optionExplanations.o2: Inbox record-type configuration does not add a Teams connected-chat record type.
optionExplanations.o3: A profile alone does not add the connection record type.
optionExplanations.o4: Knowledge enablement is different from configuring which types support connected Teams chats.

questions.prompt: A standalone extension completes a background lookup for an existing nonfocused session while the representative handles another customer. It knows the target session ID and must signal attention without immediately changing the active customer session. Which TWO API operations fit? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Retrieve the existing target session through getSession using its ID. Use requestFocus to show the target sessions notification indicator.
questions.explanation: Retrieve the intended existing session and request attention through its indicator instead of stealing focus from the current conversation.

options.text: Use getFocusedSession and assume it returns the nonfocused target.
Call focus on the target to change the active customer session immediately.
Retrieve the existing target session through getSession using its ID.
Create a duplicate session instead of signaling the existing one.
Use requestFocus to show the target sessions notification indicator.

optionExplanations.o1: The focused session is the other customer, not the target.
optionExplanations.o2: Immediate focus violates the requested no-switch behavior.
optionExplanations.o3: getSession retrieves the existing object by its known identity.
optionExplanations.o4: Duplicate creation is not attention to the existing session.
optionExplanations.o5: requestFocus signals attention when the session is not focused.

questions.prompt: A standalone provider has retrieved a corrected context value and needs future macros in that session to resolve the new slug value. It does not need to reopen a record. Which app profile manager operation owns this update?
questions.answer: updateContext, to add or modify automation-dictionary values for later macros.
questions.explanation: Update session context explicitly when subsequent macros must consume a changed value.

options.text: Pass the corrected value only as new-tab parameters and leave the existing automation dictionary unchanged.
refreshTab, because UI refresh is the documented slug mutation API.
updateContext, to add or modify automation-dictionary values for later macros.
Update the underlying record field and assume the cached session slug changes without a context update.

optionExplanations.o1: New-tab parameters are not the documented operation for updating existing automation-dictionary slugs.
optionExplanations.o2: Tab refresh is different from dictionary mutation.
optionExplanations.o3: updateContext updates slugs used by future macro invocation.
optionExplanations.o4: A data-field edit is distinct from explicitly updating the existing session dictionary for future macro values.

questions.prompt: A standalone extension finds the correct case record, but the representative switches customer sessions before the extension calls linkToConversation. Which safeguard addresses the documented target of that method?
questions.answer: Verify the intended session is focused before linking its conversation.
questions.explanation: Validate session focus at the action boundary; a valid case record alone does not select the intended ongoing conversation.

options.text: Assume the case GUID also selects the original conversation automatically.
Use the most recently opened application tab regardless of its session.
Read the newly focused conversation GUID and proceed without checking whether it is the intended customer conversation.
Verify the intended session is focused before linking its conversation.
